moved.sentence: Do not restate the line below it.

judged.note: A comment not restating the line below it is kept at SHOULD NOT with the increment-counter example and its reason (noise, a second thing to keep in sync).

moved.sentence: If a comment is needed to explain what a block does, first try a clearer name or a smaller function.

judged.note: Trying a clearer name or a smaller function first, before a what-comment, is kept at SHOULD, with 'comment what is left'.

moved.sentence: Name the source of a surprising value: the spec section, the ticket, the measurement.

judged.note: Naming the source of a surprising value is kept at SHOULD with all three example sources.

moved.sentence: These are the habits that make prose read as written by a person who knows the subject, distilled from the humanize skill's review rules.

judged.note: The framing that these are the habits of prose written by a person who knows the subject, distilled from the humanize skill's review rules, is kept in rationale and scoped to the plain-language rules.

moved.sentence: **Specifics over abstractions.** Name the thing, the number, the file.

judged.note: Specifics over abstractions (name the thing, the number, the file) is kept at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: Never make up a statistic, source or quote.

judged.note: Never making up a statistic, source or quote is kept, strengthened to MUST NOT.

moved.sentence: **Cut throat-clearing.** Do not open by restating the title or announcing what you are about to say, and do not close by summarizing what you just said.

judged.note: No throat-clearing at the open or summarizing at the close is kept at SHOULD NOT, with both halves.

moved.sentence: **Short ordinary words.** Prefer "use" to "utilize" and "show" to "demonstrate".

judged.note: Preferring short ordinary words, with both examples, is kept at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: **Do not swap synonyms to disguise a tic.** If a word is vague, rewrite the clause so it is not needed.

judged.note: Not swapping synonyms to disguise a tic, and rewriting the clause instead, is kept at SHOULD NOT.

moved.sentence: **Verbs over nominalizations.** Write "we decide" rather than "we make a decision".

judged.note: Verbs over nominalizations, with the example, is kept at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: **Active voice by default.** Passive is fine when the actor does not matter.

judged.note: Active voice by default is kept at SHOULD, with the exception for when the actor does not matter.

moved.sentence: **Hedge only real uncertainty**, and say what is uncertain.

judged.note: Hedging only real uncertainty and saying what is uncertain is kept at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: **Vary rhythm because the content calls for it**, not to hit a quota.

judged.note: Varying rhythm because the content calls for it, not to hit a quota, is kept at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: **Punctuation does a job.** Use a comma, colon, parentheses or a new sentence rather than a dash.

judged.note: Using a comma, colon, parentheses or a new sentence rather than a dash is kept at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: **Keep one tense and one register** through a passage.

judged.note: Keeping one tense and one register through a passage is kept at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: **State the premise** behind a claim, or weaken the claim to what you can support.

judged.note: Stating the premise behind a claim, or weakening it to what can be supported, is kept at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: **Visible characters only.** Never paste look-alike or invisible Unicode characters into text.

judged.note: Never pasting look-alike or invisible Unicode characters is kept, at MUST NOT.

moved.sentence: Where the host has the humanize skill, run it over prose you wrote and review its findings.

judged.note: Running the humanize skill over your prose where the host has it, and reviewing its findings, is kept at SHOULD with its condition and the by-hand fallback.

moved.sentence: When a change alters behavior, update the comments, docstrings, README sections and instruction files that describe it in that same change.

judged.note: Updating the comments, docstrings, README sections and instruction files that describe changed behavior in the same change is kept at SHOULD, with all four doc kinds.

moved.sentence: Search the docs for the names you changed, as you would search code.

judged.note: Searching the docs for changed names as you would search code is kept at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: New public behavior needs a description where users will look for it.

judged.note: New public behavior getting a description where users will look is kept at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: Removed behavior needs its description removed (see `docs-match-code`).

judged.note: Removing the description of removed behavior is kept at SHOULD with the docs-match-code reference.

moved.sentence: Both readers need the same things: exact names they can search for, the real command to run, the real path, and a statement of when a rule applies.

judged.note: The rule keeps, at SHOULD, that both readers (named as the AI agent and the human, as the old heading did) need the same things: exact searchable names, the real command, the real path, and when a rule applies.

moved.sentence: Lead with the point.

judged.note: Leading with the point is kept at SHOULD, with its reason (an agent loads partially, a person skims).

moved.sentence: Prefer concrete examples with real values over abstract descriptions.

judged.note: Preferring concrete examples with real values over abstract descriptions is kept at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: Keep one canonical term for each concept, and use it everywhere.

judged.note: One canonical term per concept, used everywhere, is kept at SHOULD with its reason.

moved.sentence: Say what is true now.

judged.note: Saying what is true now is kept at SHOULD, with leaving out narration of how it got that way.
